newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arabs need more shipping firms for petrochemicals.
newsitem.headline: Arabs need more shipping firms for petrochemicals.

text.p: A Gulf official urged Arab states on Tuesday to set up new shipping companies to cash in on the demand for transporting petrochemical products.
"We call for investments to establish new shipping firms to ship petrochemical products," Gulf Petrochemical Industries Co (GPIC) general manager Mustafa al-Sayed said.
He was speaking on the sidelines of a two-day conference on the petrochemical industry in the Arab world which ended in Bahrain earlier in the day.
Sayed also called for more Arab investment in the profitable petrochemical industry. "The industry has good profitability and good economic income, but it needs enough capital and encouragement".
Sayed said the Bahrain-based GPIC had posted around $100 million in net profits in 1994 and 1995. He declined to give 1996 figures.
"The company has paid a $30 million dividend to shareholders in the past two years while the rest went to finance a new urea plant," he added.
GPIC signed a $136 million deal last year with Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd to build a 1,700-tonne per day urea plant in Bahrain.
GPIC is owned by the Bahrain National Oil Company, Saudi Arabia's Industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp and Kuwait's Petrochemical Industries Company.
